thread:
incident-bot: :warning: Routing alert: high-frequency region fallback detected for service group 'prod-serve-large'. Flapping observed between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu. Error spike: 5xx increase, tail latency up. Auto-paging on-call.

jordan (oncall): On it. Seeing many route-change events in the router timeline. Triage started.

lee (sre): Quick dump from router decision log:
```\n[2026-03-22T09:41:02Z] router: eval group=prod-serve-large req=xyz from=us-east -> us-west reason=probe_fail probe_id=pr-9
[2026-03-22T09:41:03Z] router: eval group=prod-serve-large req=xyz from=us-west -> eu reason=probe_fail probe_id=pr-12
[2026-03-22T09:41:04Z] router: eval group=prod-serve-large req=xyz from=eu -> us-east reason=probe_ok probe_id=pr-3
[2026-03-22T09:41:05Z] router: eval group=prod-serve-large req=xyz from=us-east -> us-west reason=probe_fail probe_id=pr-9
```\nLooks like probe results are toggling every second.

anika (runtime): Confirmed. Probes for a handful of us-west runtimes return 503 on the health endpoint. Node metrics show normal CPU/GPU; however connection errors to the internal config service spiked. The health endpoint calls a permission-check API (internal-auth) which is rate-limited. If internal-auth returns 429, our health handler maps that to 503.

rafael (eng-ml): Any recent deployments that touch internal-auth or the health handler?

anika (runtime): We rolled a small canary for a telemetry agent (telemetry-sidecar v2.3) onto ~8% of nodes last night. The agent opens a config subscription to internal-auth and aggressively polls at 200ms intervals on startup until warmed. That appears to have pushed internal-auth over its soft-QPS on certain availability zones, causing 429 responses.

jordan (oncall): So root chain: telemetry canary -> internal-auth rate limiting -> health endpoint 503 -> router marks unhealthy -> low hysteresis causes flip -> cross-region oscillation.

lee (sre): Impact metrics: 4-7% 502/504 errors across prod-serve-large for ~28 minutes; p95 increased by ~350ms; about 24 paid customers with intermittent failures. Severity: P2.

jordan (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Stop the canary rollout (drain telemetry-sidecar from affected nodes), 2) Add routing dampening or enable sticky-region while we stabilize, 3) Post short customer status.

ops-pager: On call. Drafting status page: "We are investigating increased errors and latency for some requests in multiple regions. We have applied temporary routing safeguards and are rolling back a canary. No customer data loss. Updates every 20 minutes." Approve?

jordan (oncall): Approve, mention enterprise contacts.

lee (sre): Executing mitigations. 1) Scale down telemetry-sidecar daemonset patch on canary fraction:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch daemonset telemetry-sidecar --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"canary":"0"}}}}}'
```
Scaling started. 2) Tweak routing to add 45s probe dampening for prod-serve-large:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOK" \
  https://control.internal/api/routing/prod-serve-large -d '{"probe_dampen_ms":45000,"allow_cross_region_failover":false}'
```
API responded 200. :white_check_mark:

jordan (oncall): Monitoring: router flip rate dropped ~90% in 40s. Error rate trending down. Nice.

anika (runtime): Confirmed: internal-auth 429s are falling as telemetry canary scales down. Health endpoints return 200 again for those nodes.

rafael (eng-ml): We need a long-term fix: 1) telemetry agent should use exponential backoff and jitter on subscription, 2) internal-auth should expose a more informative health signal or handle subscription bursts gracefully, 3) routing should not treat 429 as hard failure for health checks (map to degraded instead).

lee (sre): Agreed. I'll open config MR to change probe->unhealthy mapping for 429/429-like responses and add hysteresis per-route.

ops-pager: Customer comms posted and enterprise contacts notified. Several customers asked for ETA on RCA.

jordan (oncall): Triage update: short-term mitigations in place (canary scaled to 0, probe dampening, sticky-region). Systems stable. Planning a post-incident review. Handoff scheduled in 40m to lee.

anika (runtime): Rolling a fix for telemetry-sidecar to add backoff/jitter and reduce startup polling frequency. Patch will be staged to canary with stricter gating. ETA 50m.

lee (sre): Action items assigned:
- Change routing probe mapping for 4xx vs 5xx (owner: lee)
- Add per-route probe dampening defaults and minimum healthy window (owner: lee)
- Telemetry-sidecar backoff/jitter and canary gating (owner: anika)
- Internal-auth load testing and graceful degrade behavior (owner: rafael)
- Update runbook for 'probe-dependency saturation' scenario (owner: jordan)

jordan (oncall): Good. Once all nodes show healthy and flip-rate stable, we'll close active paging and schedule postmortem. Current status: service restored, ongoing monitoring.

incident-bot: :bell: On-call handover in 40 minutes to lee.

ops-pager: Noted, updating status page to say: "Mitigation in place; rolling back canary and adding routing dampening. Investigating root cause."

lee (sre): Creating INC-4412 for follow-ups and RCA. I'll draft postmortem and tag owners.

jordan (oncall): Wrapping up live triage. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=P2, impact=medium, duration=~35m, mitigations=canary-scale-down, routing-dampening. Link: https://playbook/internal/incidents/2271234567

jordan (oncall): Handing to lee for post-incident work. Closing live thread at 2026-03-22T10:03:00Z.

lee (sre): Taking over. Will circulate RCA draft by EOD and schedule postmortem meeting.
